problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 7 & -9 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the General Solution of a Singular 3x3 System of Equations with One Pivot
examples.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14041677/assets/924d54c1839259b1a35fa9ed39eab97a96e538863b03f0e6833f407be98f6d01.png)

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.
examples.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 3 & 1 \\ -2 & -2 & -6 & -2 \\ 3 & 3 & 9 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & 3 & 9 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14041677/assets/36f5603649e8e185a03bf9c4e88180ec95ebb3b065e78b4d2d462b5ac2801bf4.png)

Since any numbers $x,y,z$ form a solution of the final two equations $0x+0y+0z = 0,$ we can remove these equations from the system. So, our system now consists of just a single equation:

$$
x + y + 3z = 1
$$

The basic variable is $x$, and we have two free variables $y$ and $z$. That means we need to find $x$ in terms of $y,z.$ Doing this, we get

$$
x = 1-y-3z.
$$

Therefore, the general solution is
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14041677/assets/90f271b13648e97d322d31aa29c4a9cb647dc9d5c1b7d8d0eee23875d36480ab.png)

where $y,z$ (the free variables) are arbitrary numbers.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1-y-3z \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+y[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+z[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,y,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

Geometrically, this is the equation of a plane in $\mathbb R^3$, and any point on the plane is a solution to the system.

feedback.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & -2 \\ 2 & 1 & 1 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.
feedback.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & -2 \\ 2 & 1 & 1 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & -2 \\ 2 & 1 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+0y+2z=-2 \\ 0x+y-3z=3 \\ 0x+0y+0z=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any numbers $x,y,z$ form a solution of the final equation $0x+0y+0z=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of just two equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+2z=-2 \\ y-3z=3\end{aligned}
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$ and $y,$ and we have one free variable, $z.$ That means we need to find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z.$ To do this, we apply the back substitution. 

From the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y-3z=3\,⇒\,y=3+3z\end{aligned}
$$

and from the first equation, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}x+2z=-2\,⇒\,x=-2-2z.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=-2-2z \\ y=3+3z \\ z=z\end{aligned}
$$

where $z$ (free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-2-2z \\ 3+3z \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 3 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+z[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$
